::: {.callout-important} 本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.5 Trigonometry： - sketch and use sine、cosine、tangent graphs，角度可用 degrees 或 radians； - 使用 $30^\circ$、$45^\circ$、$60^\circ$ 及相关角的 exact values； - 使用 $\sin^{-1}x$、$\cos^{-1}x$、$\tan^{-1}x$ 的 principal values； - 使用基本 trigonometric identities，解给定 interval 内的 equations； - 识别 $y=a\sin(bx)+c$、$y=a\cos(bx)+c$ 的 amplitude、period、midline 与 transformations。 下列 16 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。 ::: ## 1. Core knowledge ::: {.study-card} ### Exact values and identities $$\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12,\quad\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac12,\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\cos\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\cos\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$ $$\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1,\qquad\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}.$$ 做 identity proof 时先统一分母，再使用 $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$；解 equation 时最后必须按题目 interval 补齐所有 quadrant solutions。 ::: ::: {.formula-panel} ### Equations and graphs 若 $0\le x\le2\pi$，则 $$\sin x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi-\alpha;\quad\cos x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,2\pi-\alpha;\quad\tan x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi+\alpha.$$ 对 $y=a\sin(bx)+c$ 或 $y=a\cos(bx)+c$： $$\text{amplitude}=|a|,\qquad\text{period}=\frac{2\pi}{|b|},\qquad\text{midline }y=c.$$ ::: ## 2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q01} ### Question 1 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q7(a–b) (a) Prove $\frac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac2{\cos\theta}$. (b) Hence solve the equation when the right-hand side is $3/\sin\theta$, for $0\le\theta\le2\pi$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$\frac{(1+\sin\theta)^2+\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\frac{2+2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\boxed{\frac2{\cos\theta}}.$$ Then $2/\cos\theta=3/\sin\theta$, so $\tan\theta=3/2$. Therefore $$\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}\frac32,\ \pi+\tan^{-1}\frac32=0.983,\ 4.12\text{ rad}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q02} ### Question 2 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q2(a–b) Express $3\cos\theta=8\tan\theta$ as a quadratic in $\sin\theta$. Hence find the acute angle in degrees. **[3+2]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Multiplying by $\cos\theta$ and using $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$: $$3(1-\sin^2\theta)=8\sin\theta\Longrightarrow\boxed{3\sin^2\theta+8\sin\theta-3=0}.$$ Thus $(3\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+3)=0$. Only $\sin\theta=1/3$ is possible, so $$\boxed{\theta=\sin^{-1}\frac13=19.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q2(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q03} ### Question 3 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q9(a) $$f(x)=2-3\sin2x,\qquad g(x)=-2f(x),\qquad0\le x\le\pi.$$ State the ranges of $f$ and $g$. **[3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Because $2x$ covers a complete cycle, $-1\le\sin2x\le1$. Hence $$\boxed{-1\le f(x)\le5}.$$ Multiplying the range by $-2$ reverses the endpoints: $$\boxed{-10\le g(x)\le2}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q9(a), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q04} ### Question 4 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q7(a–b) (a) Show $\frac{\sin\theta}{1-\sin\theta}-\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=2\tan^2\theta$. (b) Hence solve the equation when the left-hand side is $8$, for $0<\theta<\pi$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}=\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\boxed{2\tan^2\theta}.$$ So $2\tan^2\theta=8$, giving $\tan\theta=\pm2$. The two solutions in $(0,\pi)$ are $$\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}2,\ \pi-\tan^{-1}2=1.107,\ 2.034\text{ rad}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q05} ### Question 5 · 9709/13/M/J/21 Q4(a–b) Show $\frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=k$ may be expressed as $\frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}=k$. Hence express $\cos x$ in terms of $k$. **[2+2]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Using $\tan x=\sin x/\cos x$, $$\frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=\frac{\sin x(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1-\cos x)}=\boxed{\frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}}.$$ Rearrange: $$1+\cos x=k(1-\cos x)\Longrightarrow\boxed{\cos x=\frac{k-1}{k+1}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching 9709_s21_ms_13.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q06} ### Question 6 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q3 Solve by factorising: $$6\cos\theta\tan\theta-3\cos\theta+4\tan\theta-2=0,\qquad0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ.$$
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$3\cos\theta(2\tan\theta-1)+2(2\tan\theta-1)=0,$$ so $(2\tan\theta-1)(3\cos\theta+2)=0$. Therefore $\tan\theta=1/2$ or $\cos\theta=-2/3$: $$\boxed{\theta=26.6^\circ\text{ or }131.8^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q3, and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q07} ### Question 7 · 9709/12/O/N/21 Q1 Solve $2\cos\theta=7-\frac3{\cos\theta}$ for $-90^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$. **[4]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Multiplying by $\cos\theta$: $$2\cos^2\theta-7\cos\theta+3=0=(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta-3).$$ The root $\cos\theta=3$ is impossible. Thus $\cos\theta=1/2$, and the symmetric interval gives $$\boxed{\theta=-60^\circ\text{ or }60^\circ}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_w21_ms_12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q08} ### Question 8 · 9709/13/O/N/21 Q7(a–b) Show that $\frac{\tan x+\cos x}{\tan x-\cos x}=k$ becomes $(k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0$. Hence solve the original equation for $k=4$, $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$. **[4+4]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Multiplying by $\cos x$ and using $\cos^2x=1-\sin^2x$ gives $$\boxed{(k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0}.$$ For $k=4$: $$5\sin^2x+3\sin x-5=0,\qquad\sin x=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{109}}{10}.$$ Only the positive root is admissible, so $$\boxed{x=48.1^\circ\text{ or }131.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_13.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w21_ms_13.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q09} ### Question 9 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q1 Solve $4\sin\theta+\tan\theta=0$ for $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$. **[3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$\sin\theta\left(4+\frac1{\cos\theta}\right)=0.$$ The endpoints are excluded, so $\sin\theta\ne0$. Therefore $\cos\theta=-1/4$, and the second-quadrant solution is $$\boxed{\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)=104.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q10} ### Question 10 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q7(a)(i–ii) (i) By expanding $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2$, find the three solutions of $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1$ for $0\le\theta\le\pi$. (ii) Hence verify that the only solutions of $\cos\theta+\sin\theta=1$ are $0$ and $\frac12\pi$. **[3+2]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ (\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1+\sin2\theta. $$ Thus $\sin2\theta=0$, giving $$\boxed{\theta=0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi}.$$ Substitution into the unsquared equation gives $1,1,-1$ respectively, so $$\boxed{\theta=0\text{ and }\frac{\pi}{2}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q7(a)(i–ii), and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q11} ### Question 11 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q5(a) The first, second and third terms of a geometric progression are $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ and $2-\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ radians is acute. Find $\theta$. **[3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer The GP condition is $\cos^2\theta=\sin\theta(2-\sin\theta)$. Since $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$, $$1-\sin^2\theta=2\sin\theta-\sin^2\theta\Longrightarrow\sin\theta=\frac12.$$ Acuteness selects $$\boxed{\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q5(a), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q12} ### Question 12 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q5(a–b) (a) Prove $\frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{1+\cos x}=-\cos x$. (b) Hence solve $\frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{2+2\cos x}=\frac14$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$\sin^2x-\cos x-1=1-\cos^2x-\cos x-1=-\cos x(1+\cos x),$$ which proves (a). In (b), the denominator is doubled, so the left side is $-\frac12\cos x$. Hence $\cos x=-1/2$ and $$\boxed{x=120^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q13} ### Question 13 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q3(a–b) (a) Show that $\frac{7\tan\theta}{\cos\theta}+12=0$ becomes $12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0$. (b) Hence solve the original equation for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Multiplying by $\cos^2\theta$ gives $7\sin\theta+12\cos^2\theta=0$. Replacing $\cos^2\theta$ by $1-\sin^2\theta$ gives $$\boxed{12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0}.$$ The factors are $(3\sin\theta+4)(4\sin\theta-3)$, so $\sin\theta=3/4$. Therefore $$\boxed{\theta=48.6^\circ\text{ or }131.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q14} ### Question 14 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q4(a–b) (a) Show that $\cos x(7\tan x-5\cos x)=1$ can be written as $a\sin^2x+b\sin x+c=0$. (b) Hence solve it for $0^\circShow detailed mark scheme answer $$7\sin x-5\cos^2x=1\Longrightarrow7\sin x-5(1-\sin^2x)=1,$$ so $$5\sin^2x+7\sin x-6=0=(5\sin x-3)(\sin x+2).$$ Only $\sin x=3/5$ is valid. Hence $$\boxed{x=\sin^{-1}\frac35=36.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q15} ### Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q8(a–b) (a) $\beta$ is between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ and $\sin\beta=a$. Express $\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta$ in terms of $a$. (b) Solve $\sin^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=4\sin\theta+3$ for $0^\circ<\theta<360^\circ$. **[3+5]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer In quadrant II, $\cos\beta=-\sqrt{1-a^2}$. Thus $$\boxed{\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta=\frac{a^2}{1-a^2}+3a\sqrt{1-a^2}}.$$ For (b), use $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$: $$\sin^2\theta+2(1-\sin^2\theta)=4\sin\theta+3\Longrightarrow\sin^2\theta+4\sin\theta+1=0.$$ The valid root is $\sin\theta=-2+\sqrt3$, giving $$\boxed{\theta=195.6^\circ\text{ or }344.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q16} ### Question 16 · 9709/13/O/N/24 Q4 Solve $4\sin^4\theta+12\sin^2\theta-7=0$ for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$. **[4]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Let $u=\sin^2\theta$. Then $4u^2+12u-7=0$, so $$u=\frac{-12\pm16}{8}=1/2\text{ or }-3.$$ Reject $u=-3$. Hence $\sin^2\theta=1/2$, and $$\boxed{\theta=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ,\ 225^\circ,\ 315^\circ}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4, and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf.
::: ## 3. Quick checklist - [ ] exact values and quadrant signs - [ ] $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$ - [ ] $\tan x=\sin x/\cos x$ - [ ] identities before numerical substitution - [ ] all solutions in the stated interval - [ ] amplitude, period and midline

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q5(a), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q12} ### Question 12 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q5(a–b) (a) Prove $\frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{1+\cos x}=-\cos x$. (b) Hence solve $\frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{2+2\cos x}=\frac14$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$\sin^2x-\cos x-1=1-\cos^2x-\cos x-1=-\cos x(1+\cos x),$$ which proves (a). In (b), the denominator is doubled, so the left side is $-\frac12\cos x$. Hence $\cos x=-1/2$ and $$\boxed{x=120^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q13} ### Question 13 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q3(a–b) (a) Show that $\frac{7\tan\theta}{\cos\theta}+12=0$ becomes $12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0$. (b) Hence solve the original equation for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$. **[3+3]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Multiplying by $\cos^2\theta$ gives $7\sin\theta+12\cos^2\theta=0$. Replacing $\cos^2\theta$ by $1-\sin^2\theta$ gives $$\boxed{12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0}.$$ The factors are $(3\sin\theta+4)(4\sin\theta-3)$, so $\sin\theta=3/4$. Therefore $$\boxed{\theta=48.6^\circ\text{ or }131.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q14} ### Question 14 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q4(a–b) (a) Show that $\cos x(7\tan x-5\cos x)=1$ can be written as $a\sin^2x+b\sin x+c=0$. (b) Hence solve it for $0^\circShow detailed mark scheme answer $$7\sin x-5\cos^2x=1\Longrightarrow7\sin x-5(1-\sin^2x)=1,$$ so $$5\sin^2x+7\sin x-6=0=(5\sin x-3)(\sin x+2).$$ Only $\sin x=3/5$ is valid. Hence $$\boxed{x=\sin^{-1}\frac35=36.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q15} ### Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q8(a–b) (a) $\beta$ is between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ and $\sin\beta=a$. Express $\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta$ in terms of $a$. (b) Solve $\sin^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=4\sin\theta+3$ for $0^\circ<\theta<360^\circ$. **[3+5]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer In quadrant II, $\cos\beta=-\sqrt{1-a^2}$. Thus $$\boxed{\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta=\frac{a^2}{1-a^2}+3a\sqrt{1-a^2}}.$$ For (b), use $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$: $$\sin^2\theta+2(1-\sin^2\theta)=4\sin\theta+3\Longrightarrow\sin^2\theta+4\sin\theta+1=0.$$ The valid root is $\sin\theta=-2+\sqrt3$, giving $$\boxed{\theta=195.6^\circ\text{ or }344.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.
::: ::: {.question-card #p1-trig-q16} ### Question 16 · 9709/13/O/N/24 Q4 Solve $4\sin^4\theta+12\sin^2\theta-7=0$ for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$. **[4]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Let $u=\sin^2\theta$. Then $4u^2+12u-7=0$, so $$u=\frac{-12\pm16}{8}=1/2\text{ or }-3.$$ Reject $u=-3$. Hence $\sin^2\theta=1/2$, and $$\boxed{\theta=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ,\ 225^\circ,\ 315^\circ}.$$
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4, and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf.
